tagline: Innovate to transform the lives of patients and their families
hero_kpi_rationale: Jazz's growth is driven by recent and upcoming product launches in high-unmet-need rare diseases (Ziihera, Modeyso), making pipeline progression the key value driver rather than traditional pharma metrics.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Revenue is primarily driven by rare disease therapies such as Xywav, Epidiolex, and Zepzelca. Growth is supported by clinical adoption and international launches.
kpis.signal: Stable growth driven by Xywav and Epidiolex.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.description: The margin reflects a targeted business model in rare diseases with a low number of prescribers.
kpis.signal: High margin for an efficient biopharma model.

kpis.name: R&D as % of Revenue
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenue invested in research and development.
kpis.description: Jazz maintains a high level of R&D investment to develop new therapies for rare diseases.
kpis.signal: Sustained investment in rare disease pipeline.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Margin after cost of goods sold.
kpis.description: Products are highly differentiated, enabling high prices and strong margins.
kpis.signal: Very high margin typical of specialized biotechs.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.description: Investments are primarily related to commercial and logistics infrastructure.
kpis.signal: Moderate Capex, consistent with a biopharma model without heavy manufacturing.

kpis.name: Total Headcount
kpis.description: Headcount supports global commercial, R&D, and regulatory activities.
kpis.signal: Stable headcount for a targeted commercial model.

kpis.name: Ziihera Revenue (first year)
kpis.explanation: Sales of the new liver cancer drug.
kpis.description: Ziihera, launched in December 2024 in the United States, generated $150 million in revenue in 2025, indicating rapid adoption.
kpis.signal: Successful launch in an untreated rare cancer segment.

kpis.name: Xywav Revenue for IH
kpis.explanation: Portion of Xywav sales related to idiopathic hypersomnia.
kpis.description: Since its launch for IH in November 2021, Xywav has gained traction with $400M in revenue in 2025. As of end-2025, approximately 5,225 IH patients were on Xywav.
kpis.signal: Rapid growth in the IH indication, which remains underdiagnosed.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Total revenue extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 declared fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Total revenue of $0.476 Bn last fiscal year (FY2018).

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.description: Net income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 declared fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Net income of -$0.356 Bn last fiscal year (FY2025).

risks.title: High Leverage
risks.score_rationale: The company has high debt levels following acquisitions (GW Pharma), which could impact its financial flexibility and access to capital. The 10-K explicitly highlights risks related to debt servicing.

risks.title: Liquidity Risks and Debt Servicing
risks.score_rationale: The company could face difficulties if it is unable to generate sufficient cash flow to repay its debt. Capacity depends heavily on sales of key products.

risks.title: Dependence on Key Products
risks.score_rationale: Growth is highly reliant on Xywav and Epidiolex. Loss of market share or regulatory issues could significantly impact growth and profitability.

risks.title: Regulatory and Drug Approval Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company is subject to strict FDA and other regulatory requirements. Recent launches (Ziihera, Modeyso) are under accelerated or conditional approval, requiring confirmatory trials.

risks.title: Competitive Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company operates in a competitive market. Example: Lumryz (Avadel), launched in May 2023 for narcolepsy with high-sodium oxybate, although Xywav retains cardiovascular safety advantages.

risks.title: Capital Needs for Future Growth
risks.score_rationale: To continue growing, Jazz will need to make substantial investments in acquisitions, licensing, clinical trials, and commercial expansion, which could limit financial flexibility.

ai_positioning.summary: Jazz Pharmaceuticals does not mention artificial intelligence (AI) or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing.
